newsitem.title: UK: Clinton - US budget leaves no room for big spending.
newsitem.headline: Clinton - US budget leaves no room for big spending.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton said on Thursday his budget agreement with Congress left little room for major new spending programmes.
"Does it allow for big spending programmes? No it doesn't," he told reporters at Downing St, official residence of British Prime Minister Tony Blair.
"If we want to spend any more money in the next 3-1/2 years, we either have to grow the economy or raise the money. That is what a balanced budget is for. I support that," he said.

But he added that the budget included the biggest increase in education spending in a generation, a big rise in environmental protection and $17 billion to insure children who do not have health insurance.

Last week, the United States Senate delayed passage of a balanced budget agreement. Final approval by both chambers of Congress will have to wait until June 3, whent they return from a week-long recess.
Clinton said he wanted to keep unemployment at or under five percent over the next four years more than anything else.

But he added: "I want us to be in a position...where we can't launch a big new programme unless we raise the money for it or grow the economy to fund it. That is the fiscally responsible way to do it."
Blair, Britain's new Prime Minister, echoed those comments.
